prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System (CBTC): underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering-hour; separation/authority/regulation protection. Metro Operations Control System (Lantern), non-vital, sends Crew Login Token Bundle; displays positions/routes/alarms/performance/station-platform states using workstation identifiers; previews regulation/action/train/recovery before confirmation; reconciles timetable-deviation/closure/crowding before passenger publication. Line Traffic Controller owns regulation, issues Temporary Speed Restriction Notice, logs incidents/recovery; station holds constrain departure, not locking. Dispatch requires positive confirmation/cancellation. Voice Dispatch Console shows calling identity/platform/hold-reason; Revenue Train Operator reads back, reports conditions/hazards; voice never replaces safety validation. North District Zone Controller (Marble)/South District Zone Controller (Orchid) manage districts/turnbacks/East-West approaches; transfer requires ownership/overlap/receiver-validation; restrictive evidence governs. East Junction Interlocking (Falcon)/West Junction Interlocking retain locking; authority requires proved/locked points/overlaps/flanks; release requires detection/correspondence/opposing-route checks. Correspondence loss reduces authority. Axle counters independently prove availability; East sends Axle Counter Reset Request, forbidden under route/approach locking. Maple (unidentified) records clearance. West sends Route Release Exception List; unresolved hazards persist. Platform Screen Door Controller produces Platform Door Status Snapshot: closed/locked/bypassed/inhibited/faulted; not route-proof; constrains arrival/dwell/departure; direction-compatible doors required; Marble suppresses unsafe-berth departure. Atlas Onboard Controller (Kestrel): authenticated activation; initialization/protected-manual/automatic-train/fallback/cutout; validates authority/context/token, rejects stale acknowledgements, enforces profiles; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log; reports door-enable-side/berth/readiness. Dual Channel Odometer supplies distance/speed/boundary-confidence; divergence increases uncertainty/separation. Train Radio Modem uses Wayside Radio Access Network (Saffron), sends Radio Handover Audit File; degradation retains validated-authority; loss permits holds. Saffron maintains station-message paths. Cryptographic Key Management Appliance checks certificates/clocks, produces Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack during approved-maintenance; modem uses pack before renewed-sessions. Safety Data Communication Network separates safety-station/nonvital-passenger messages. Service Timetable Server supplies planned-context; changes require approval/controller-verification. Passenger Information Gateway receives timetable-reconciled

New part:
S150: During degraded operation, the CBTC system favours restrictive platform states and requires explicit controller action before restoring automatic departure support at the affected station.
S151: Diagnostics and maintenance for the Greenvale Metro communications-based train control system are organised around prompt event collection, controlled remote access, and traceable engineering decisions.
S152: Each safety-related part records time-stamped events for state changes, command acceptance, rejected commands, communication loss, and local protective actions.
S153: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server receives event streams from fixed and onboard equipment through monitored interfaces that do not allow maintenance traffic to alter train movement authority.
S154: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server uses the checksum log to compare stored braking data identifiers against the expected maintenance baseline for the affected train.
S155: Remote diagnostic sessions are initiated by a Signal Maintenance Engineer and are limited to read-only observation unless an approved maintenance window authorises a specific intervention.
S156: The Cyber Security Officer reviews privileged diagnostic access logs and confirms that remote connections use current credentials and approved encryption settings.
S157: The Line Traffic Controller receives the Route Release Exception List during incident triage and uses it to check whether a release anomaly could affect service recovery decisions.
S158: Marble records controller health, interface state, and fallback mode transitions in a form that can be correlated with adjacent wayside and operations records.
S159: The South District Zone Controller maintains comparable diagnostic coverage so that boundary events can be reviewed without relying on a single source of evidence.
S160: The East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking report route command histories, point detection changes, and protective lock status to support failure localisation.
S161: The Atlas Onboard Controller stores onboard fault codes, movement authority acceptance records, propulsion cutback requests, and train interface exceptions for later retrieval.
S162: The Dual Channel Odometer provides distance and speed plausibility information that is retained with trainborne diagnostic records after any odometry disagreement.
S163: The Train Radio Modem records bearer loss, reconnection timing, signal quality indicators, and message retry counts needed to distinguish radio coverage issues from equipment faults.
S164: The Wayside Radio Access Network and Safety Data Communication Network provide communication performance records that are compared with controller logs during network-related investigations.
S165: The Metro Operations Control System displays selected fault summaries to the Line Traffic Controller but does not expose detailed maintenance commands at the traffic control workstation.
S166: A Revenue Train Operator reports observed cab indications, train handling effects, and passenger service impacts using the operational reporting channel defined for degraded service.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
